```regex
^[0-9]{5}(-[0-9]{4})?$
```

This matches `12345` and `12345-6789`. The anchors `^` and `$` make it match the whole string, so `123456` and `12345-678` are rejected. I used `[0-9]` instead of `\d` because `\d` can match non-ASCII digits in some engines.

It checks the format only. It doesn't check that the code is assigned, since valid ZIPs run from 00501 to 99950.
